text.p01: To everyone who looks after the place they love: you can start with one small stick. A story about looking after the place you love. In Aotearoa New Zealand, Māori speak of kaitiakitanga: being a guardian of the land and the sea. We look after them the way those before us did, so that those who come after us can love them too.
text.p03: On a beach by the big blue sea lived Tama, the littlest of the little blue penguins, with a fluffy tuft still on his head.
text.p04: Every evening, the penguins swam home and waddled up the sandy path to their burrows under the bushes. Pitter-pat, pitter-pat, all the way home.
text.p05: In the bushes above the beach lived Tama's best friend, Aroha, a young kiwi who carried a shiny rainbow shell everywhere she went.
text.p06: Every night, they raced up and down the sandy path together. "This is the best beach in the whole wide world!" said Tama.
text.p07: Then one night, a big storm blew. In the morning, the path was covered with tangled seaweed, driftwood, sticks and a lost flip-flop.
text.p08: That evening, the penguins tripped and stumbled all the way home. "Oof! Ouch! Who made this mess?" they grumbled. "Someone should clean it up!"
text.p09: But nobody did. And every day, the sea washed up a little more. "It's not my mess," said Tama, and he hopped right over it.
text.p10: Then one evening, a tiny chick got stuck behind a big piece of driftwood. Tama helped her over. "Thank you," she peeped, and waddled home.
text.p11: That night, Tama couldn't sleep. His grandma's grandma had walked this path. One day, that tiny chick's chicks would walk it too.
text.p12: "It doesn't matter whose mess it is," said Tama. "Every day, this path brings us home. Now I'm going to look after it."
text.p13: Aroha giggled. "But you're the littlest penguin in the world!" "Then I'll start little," said Tama. And he picked up one small stick.
text.p14: The next day, he moved two sticks. Then a ball of seaweed. Then a bottle cap. Pitterpat, pitter-pat, up and down the path.
text.p15: Aroha watched him for a while. Then she put down her rainbow shell and pushed the big driftwood away with her strong legs.
text.p16: Together they rolled away the seaweed and carried the lost flip-flop far up the beach. Nobody else even noticed. But Tama didn't mind one bit.
text.p17: Every single day, Tama checked his path. When the sea brought new things, he just smiled and cleared them away. Pitter-pat, pitter-pat.
text.p18: He lined the edges with smooth white shells that glowed in the moonlight, so everyone could find their way home in the dark.
text.p19: One morning, three little chicks peeked out of their burrow. "What are you doing?" they asked. "Looking after our path," said Tama.
text.p20: "Can we help too?" they asked. Tama smiled and showed them how to carry one small stick each. "Start little," he said.
text.p21: That night, the whole colony swam home under a big silver moon. The white shells glowed. Pitter-pat, pitter-pat, pitter-pat!
text.p22: Nobody tripped at all. Behind everyone came the three little chicks, each carrying one small stick. Tama's heart felt as big as the sea.
text.p23: Every day after that, Tama and his little helpers looked after the path, and the path brought everyone safely home.
text.p24: Pitter-pat, pitter-pat. One day, those chicks will teach their own chicks too. Look after the world, the way it looks after you. The End
text.cover: The Littlest Guardian. A Story About Looking After the Place You Love
